claim: DNA methylation is an essential epigenetic mark.
source_text: DNA methylation is an essential epigenetic mark whose role in gene regulation and its dependency on genomic sequence and environment are not fully understood.
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citation to Li et al., 1992 in the Introduction section and represents established scientific consensus about DNA methylation.

claim: The association between DNA methylation and gene expression variation among individuals are likely due to different mechanisms from those establishing methylation-expression patterns during differentiation.
source_text: We find that the association between DNA methylation and gene expression variation among individuals are likely due to different mechanisms from those establishing methylation-expression patterns during differentiation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on data analysis from the GenCord cohort and represents an inference drawn from comparing inter-individual variation with differentiation patterns.

claim: Cell-type differential DNA methylation may delineate a platform in which local inter-individual changes may respond to or act in gene regulation.
source_text: Furthermore, cell-type differential DNA methylation may delineate a platform in which local inter-individual changes may respond to or act in gene regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the data showing relationships between cell-type differentiation and inter-individual variation in the study.

claim: Unlike genetic regulatory variation, DNA methylation alone does not significantly drive allele specific expression.
source_text: We show that unlike genetic regulatory variation, DNA methylation alone does not significantly drive allele specific expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the allele-specific expression analysis presented in the manuscript, comparing effects of genetic variation versus DNA methylation.

claim: DNA methylation has both a passive and active role in regulatory interactions influencing gene expression.
source_text: Finally, inferred mechanistic relationships using genetic variation as well as correlations with TF abundance reveal both a passive and active role of DNA methylation to regulatory interactions influencing gene expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by Bayesian network analysis and transcription factor correlation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: DNA methylation in vertebrates occurs most commonly in cytosines that are adjacent to guanines (CpG sites).
source_text: DNA methylation in vertebrates occurs most commonly in cytosines that are adjacent to guanines (CpG sites).
evidence_reasoning: This represents established scientific knowledge about DNA methylation patterns in vertebrates.

claim: Mammalian DNA methylation levels are generally high, although CpG rich regions, called CpG islands (CGI), appear mostly unmethylated.
source_text: Mammalian DNA methylation levels are generally high, although CpG rich regions, called CpG islands (CGI), appear mostly unmethylated
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (Bird, 2002; Weber et al., 2007; Lister et al., 2009) and represents established knowledge.

claim: DNA methylation can be positively correlated to gene transcription when found in gene bodies.
source_text: Even though it was originally reported to be involved in gene silencing (Holliday and Pugh, 1975; Riggs, 1975), more recent studies have found that DNA methylation can also be positively correlated to gene transcription when found in gene bodies
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Hellman and Chess, 2007 and Lister et al., 2009.

claim: Genetic variation influences DNA methylation levels in different cell-types.
source_text: Furthermore, studies looking at natural DNA methylation variation in human populations have shown that genetic variation influences DNA methylation levels in different cell-types
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Gibbs et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2010; Bell et al., 2011.

claim: The study identified 2115-3372 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) at 10% FDR using a 1 Mb window.
source_text: At 10% FDR, we identify 2115–3372 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) using a 1 Mb window to either side of the TSS.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of quantitative results from the eQTL analysis performed in the study.

claim: The study discovered 14,189-32,318 methylation QTLs (mQTLs) using a 5-kb window.
source_text: We discover 14,189–32,318 methylation QTLs (mQTLs) using a 5-kb window to either side of the CpG site.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of quantitative results from the mQTL analysis performed in the study.

claim: The study found 1541-17,267 significant expression to methylation associations (eQTMs) using a 50-kb window around the TSS.
source_text: We find 1541–17,267 significant expression to methylation associations (eQTMs) using a 50-kb window around the TSS; these pertain to 596–3838 genes and 970–6846 CpG sites
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of quantitative results from the eQTM analysis performed in the study.

claim: DNA methylation at promoter regions correlates negatively with gene expression levels when looking at comparisons across genes.
source_text: DNA methylation at promoter regions is widely known to correlate negatively with gene expression levels when looking at comparisons across genes
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as widely known and is also supported by data shown in the manuscript's figures.

claim: As the level of cell-type methylation differentiation increases, a larger proportion of sites are associated to gene expression (eQTMs) and affected by genetic variation (mQTLs).
source_text: We find that as differentiation per methylation site increases, a higher proportion of eQTMs and mQTLs are observed
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the analysis shown in Figure 2B and statistical tests reported.

claim: The tissue differentiation level of methylation sites involved in eQTMs is significantly higher than for non-eQTM sites.
source_text: This is statistically supported by the fact that the tissue differentiation level of methylation sites involved in eQTMs and mQTLs is significantly higher than for non-eQTM and non-mQTL sites, respectively (all p values<2.2 × 10−16, Wilcoxon test
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis (Wilcoxon test) of the data with reported p-values.

claim: There is a significant increased presence of negative compared to positive eQTMs in CTCF binding sites, enhancers and promoters.
source_text: We find a significant increased presence of negative compared to positive eQTMs in CTCF binding sites, enhancers and promoters, with this increase being higher in non-CpG island (CGI) promoters compared to CGI promoters
evidence_reasoning: This is based on analysis of genomic feature overlaps with eQTMs as shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There is a significant depletion of mQTLs in CGI promoters.
source_text: Interestingly, we discover a significant depletion of mQTLs in CGI promoters
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 2D with Fisher's exact test.

claim: There is a significant enrichment of mQTLs in non-CGI promoters.
source_text: and a significant enrichment of mQTLs in non-CGI promoters
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 2D with Fisher's exact test.

claim: Methylation sites in non-CGI promoters are under a stronger genetic control than at CGI promoters.
source_text: This shows that methylation sites in non-CGI promoters are under a stronger genetic control than at CGI promoters, where methylation is in general robustly maintained at low levels.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the mQTL enrichment/depletion patterns observed in the data.

claim: eQTLs are significantly enriched in CpG islands.
source_text: Nevertheless, genetic variation in CpG islands commonly affects gene expression, since we find that eQTLs are significantly enriched at these genomic regions (all p values<0.03).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical analysis with reported p-values.

claim: Allele specific expression is significantly driven by genetic variation.
source_text: The difference between distributions is significant in all cell-types with p<2.2 × 10−16, p=2.7 × 10−15 and p=3.0 × 10−8 in fibroblasts (F), LCLs (L) and T-cells (T), respectively (Wilcoxon test). This strongly indicates that allele specific expression is significantly driven by genetic variation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison of allelic imbalance between heterozygotes and homozygotes for eQTLs.

claim: Allele specific expression is not significantly driven by DNA methylation that is not affected by genetic variation.
source_text: The difference between distributions is not significant in any cell-type, with p=0.79, p=0.42 and p=0.49 in F, L, T, respectively... This shows that allele specific expression is not significantly driven by DNA methylation that is not affected by genetic variation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by statistical comparison showing no significant difference in allelic imbalance between homomethylated and semimethylated states.

claim: Synergistic interactions between genetic variants and DNA methylation on gene expression are enriched in LCLs and T-cells.
source_text: Synergistic interactions are enriched in LCLs and T-cells (Figure 3B) with π1 being 4.3% and 9.3% (all p<0.001)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by linear regression analysis testing interaction terms with permutation-based significance assessment.

claim: In fibroblasts, the observed π1 for synergistic interactions is 12.4%, which is 7.2 times larger than the top permuted π1.
source_text: In fibroblasts, although the p value distribution is not above the 95th confidence limit (Figure 3B), the observed π1 is 12.4% (p<0.001), 7.2 times larger than the top permuted π1, which suggests a significant enrichment of interactions.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on statistical analysis comparing observed π1 to permutation-based null distribution.

claim: The study found 3, 91 and 14 individually significant interactions in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively, at 10% FDR.
source_text: Finally, we find 3, 91 and 14 individually significant interactions in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively, at 10% false discovery rate (FDR).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of significant results from the interaction analysis.

claim: Three possible causative models exist for mechanistic relationships between genetic variation, DNA methylation and gene expression: INDEP, SME, and SEM.
source_text: We used Bayesian Network (BN) construction and relative likelihood (see 'Materials and methods') to test which of the three possible causative models depicted in
evidence_reasoning: This represents the analytical framework used to infer causal relationships from the data.

claim: All three types of models (INDEP, SME and SEM) are present in the three cell-types.
source_text: The three types of models (INDEP, SME and SEM) are present in the three cell-types, suggesting that DNA methylation can have both active and passive roles in gene regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on Bayesian network analysis results shown in Figure 4B, with inference about the implications.

claim: There is a strong enrichment of significant TF-methylation associations, with π1 being 18%, 9% and 25%, in fibroblasts, LCL, and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: We found a strong enrichment of significant TF-methylation associations, with π1 being 18%, 9% and 25%, in fibroblasts, LCL, and T-cells, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is based on correlation analysis between TF expression levels and DNA methylation at their binding sites.

claim: At 10% FDR, significant associations were found for 27, 47 and 99 different TFs in fibroblasts, LCL and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: At 10% FDR, we find significant associations for 27, 47 and 99 different TFs in fibroblasts, LCL and T-cells, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of significant results from TF-methylation correlation analysis.

claim: There is an enrichment of low p values for interactions between genetic variants and TF abundance on DNA methylation levels, with π1 estimated at 15% of true positives.
source_text: Despite the limited number of cases that could be tested (N = 114), we find an enrichment of low p values for such interactions, with π1 estimated at 15% of true positives
evidence_reasoning: This is based on linear regression analysis testing interactions between SNPs and TF abundance on methylation.

claim: TF levels could be influencing DNA methylation and gene expression levels simultaneously.
source_text: These results suggest that TF levels could be influencing DNA methylation and gene expression levels simultaneously.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the TF-methylation correlation results and interaction analyses.

claim: Non-genetically determined DNA methylation is rarely allelic but rather defined at the whole cell level.
source_text: Additionally, our results suggest that non-genetically determined DNA methylation is rarely allelic but rather defined at the whole cell level.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the allele-specific expression analysis showing no significant effect of methylation on ASE.

claim: When a population of cells is observed to be semimethylated, the most likely scenario is that only a fraction of the cells are fully methylated rather than one of the alleles in each of the cells is methylated.
source_text: That is, when we observe a population of cells to be semimethylated the most likely scenario is that only a fraction of the cells are fully methylated rather than one of the alleles in each of the cells is methylated.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the allele-specific expression results regarding the nature of semimethylation.

claim: Methylation sites that represent a repressive state with respect to tissue differentiation can also participate in positive and negative associations with gene expression when looking at inter-individual variability.
source_text: Further, we show that methylation sites that represent a repressive state with respect to tissue differentiation can also participate in positive and negative associations with gene expression when looking at inter-individual variability.
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the analysis showing both positive and negative eQTMs at differentiated sites.

claim: DNA methylation emerges both as marker and determinant of cellular identity.
source_text: DNA methylation as a whole emerges both as marker and determinant of cellular identity and may provide a platform by which genetic variation and other variable factors among individuals (e.g., TFs) exert their effect to differentially influence cellular processes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis and interpretation of multiple findings from the study regarding DNA methylation's roles.

claim: The GenCord collection consists of umbilical cord and cord blood samples from 204 newborn babies.
source_text: We collected umbilical cord and cord blood samples from 204 newborn babies, from which we derived three cell-types: fibroblasts, lymphoblastoid cells and T-cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct description of the study cohort and sample collection.

claim: Three cell-types were derived from the samples: fibroblasts, lymphoblastoid cells and T-cells.
source_text: from which we derived three cell-types: fibroblasts, lymphoblastoid cells and T-cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct description of the cell types studied.

claim: Genotyping, RNA-sequencing and DNA methylation levels were assayed for the samples.
source_text: Genotyping, RNA-sequencing and DNA methylation levels were assayed.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental assays performed in the study.

claim: The promoter proximal region was defined from -1kb to +2kb relative to the TSS based on the region where expressed genes have lower methylation levels than non-expressed genes.
source_text: Based on the region where expressed genes have lower methylation levels than non-expressed genes, the promoter proximal region of our analyses was defined from -1kb to +2kb relative to the TSS.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a methodological decision based on observed methylation patterns in the data.

claim: Differentially methylated regions among cell-types play important roles in cell differentiation and tissue-specific regulation.
source_text: Differentially methylated regions among cell-types have been shown to play important roles in cell differentiation and tissue-specific regulation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Meissner et al., 2008; Schmidl et al., 2009; Hodges et al., 2011; Li et al., 2012.

claim: The establishment of differentially methylated regions during development could be delineating a backbone where local inter-individual changes may occur.
source_text: This could indicate that the establishment of differentially methylated regions during development could be delineating a backbone where local inter-individual changes may occur.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation of the finding that differentiated sites are more likely to be eQTMs and mQTLs.

claim: The role of DNA methylation can be highly dependent on the genomic and functional context.
source_text: Overall, these results suggest that the role of DNA methylation can be highly dependent on the genomic and functional context.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the context-specific analyses showing different patterns in CGI vs non-CGI promoters and other genomic features.

claim: TFs can influence DNA methylation levels near their binding sites.
source_text: It has been shown in mice (Stadler et al., 2011) that TFs can influence DNA methylation levels near their binding sites (TFBSs).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Stadler et al., 2011.

claim: By correlating expression levels of TFs with DNA methylation at their TFBSs in different cell-types, this pattern has also been observed for some TFs in human tissues.
source_text: In addition, by correlating expression levels of TFs with DNA methylation at their TFBSs in different cell-types, this pattern has also been observed for some TFs in human tissues (Thurman et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Thurman et al., 2012.

claim: DNA methylation can be linked to genetic variation and can participate in gene regulation in a passive manner.
source_text: This picture shows how DNA methylation can be linked to genetic variation, and can participate in gene regulation in a passive manner.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis of findings from the TF-methylation analyses and causal modeling.

claim: The relationships between genetic variation, DNA methylation and gene expression can be of different nature depending on tissue and genomic region.
source_text: This scenario is quite different from the often-assumed simple model of genetic variation affecting the epigenome, which in turn affects the transcriptome, and furthermore these relationships can be of different nature depending on tissue and genomic region.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the multiple types of causal models identified and context-specific patterns observed.

claim: Properly characterizing the relationships between genetic variation, epigenetics and gene expression will enhance our understanding of genome function and complex disease.
source_text: This is likely to be true for other epigenetic mechanisms as well, and properly characterizing these relationships will enhance our understanding of genome function and complex disease.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the broader implications of the research findings.

claim: The study used the Illumina 2.5M Omni chip for genotyping 204 individuals.
source_text: We extracted DNA from LCLs with the QIAamp DNA Blood Mini Kit (Qiagen, Venlo, The Netherlands) and genotyped the 204 individuals with the Illumina 2.5M Omni chip.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the genotyping methodology used in the study.

claim: Imputation was performed with Beagle v3.3.2 into 21 million European panel SNPs of the 1000 genomes March 2012 release.
source_text: We performed the imputation with Beagle v3.3.2 (Browning and Browning, 2009), into 21 million European panel SNPs of the 1000 genomes March 2012 release
evidence_reasoning: This describes the imputation methodology used in the study.

claim: After filtering, the study had a total of 6.9 million SNPs.
source_text: From the final output, we required an R2 ≥ 0.9. This yielded a total of 6.9 million SNPs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the number of SNPs after quality control filtering.

claim: The 49-bp sequenced paired-end reads were mapped to the reference genome GRCh37 with BWA v0.5.9.
source_text: Afterwards, the 49-bp sequenced paired-end reads were mapped to the reference genome (Lander et al., 2001) GRCh37 with BWA v0.5.9
evidence_reasoning: This describes the RNA-seq read mapping methodology.

claim: The study used the Illumina 450k Infinium HD Methylation Assay to measure DNA methylation.
source_text: BC-DNA was then processed through the 450K Illumina Infinium HD Methylation Assay (Illumina, San Diego, CA) according to manufacturer's instructions.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the DNA methylation assay methodology used in the study.

claim: From the 482,421 CpG sites assayed, filtering yielded a total of 416,118 CpG sites to work with.
source_text: From the 482,421 CpG sites assayed, we filtered out probes with 1000 genomes SNPs or indels at European minor allele frequency >5% and then any other probes that had any of the final set of SNPs used in our study. This yielded a total of 416,118 CpG sites to work with.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the number of CpG sites after quality control filtering.

claim: The β-value represents the percentage of methylation per site.
source_text: The β-value is defined as the proportion of fluorescent signal from the methylated allele over the total fluorescent signal (methylated and unmethylated alleles); this represents the percentage of methylation per site
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of the β-value metric used in DNA methylation studies, supported by citation.

claim: Spearman rank correlations were performed between SNP genotypes and exon expression levels (eQTLs) in 183-185 samples using a 1-MB window.
source_text: We performed Spearman rank correlations (SRC) between (x and y variables): SNP genotypes and exon expression levels (eQTLs) in 183–185 samples using a 1-MB window to either side of the TSS
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used for eQTL analysis.

claim: Spearman rank correlations were performed between SNP genotypes and CpG site methylation levels (mQTLs) in 66-111 samples using a 5-kb window.
source_text: SNP genotypes and CpG site methylation levels (mQTLs) in 66–111 samples using a 5-kb window to either side of the CpG site
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used for mQTL analysis.

claim: Spearman rank correlations were performed between CpG site methylation levels and exon expression levels (eQTMs) in 66-118 samples using a 50-kb window.
source_text: CpG site methylation levels and exon expression levels (eQTMs) in 66–118 samples using a 50-kb window to either side of the TSS.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used for eQTM analysis.

claim: The coefficient of variation was used as a measure of DNA methylation differentiation level because it is a variability measure that controls for the mean methylation.
source_text: We have used the coefficient of variation (CV) as a measure of DNA methylation differentiation level, as it is a variability measure that controls for the mean methylation.
evidence_reasoning: This explains the rationale for the methodological choice of using coefficient of variation.

claim: Bayesian networks are directed acyclic graphs where nodes represent random variables and edges represent the conditional dependences among nodes.
source_text: Bayesian networks (BN) are directed acyclic graphs where nodes represent random variables and edges represent the conditional dependences among nodes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of Bayesian networks, representing established statistical methodology.

claim: The direction of edges in Bayesian networks can be interpreted as a causal relationship.
source_text: The direction of the edges between two nodes can be interpreted as a causal relationship.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a standard interpretation of Bayesian network structure.

claim: Bayesian networks have been used before to infer causality in genetic problems.
source_text: BN have been used before to infer causality in genetic problems (Schadt et al., 2005; Zhu et al., 2008).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous studies using Bayesian networks for causal inference.

claim: The Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) score was used to compare networks of different complexities.
source_text: Since different networks have different complexities, it is common to use a score that takes into account the network complexity instead of the raw likelihood to compare the networks. We used the R package bnlearn (Scutari, 2010) to calculate the maximum likelihood of the networks and the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) score.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the statistical methodology used for comparing Bayesian network models.

claim: From the total number of tests, 61%, 36% and 27% were called as high confidence in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: From the total number of tests, 61%, 36% and 27% were called as high confidence (HC) in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the proportion of high confidence causal model calls.

claim: The number of expressed TFs in each cell-type is 94, 106 and 105 in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: The number of expressed TFs in each cell-type is 94, 106 and 105, comprising 666, 851 and 776 exons in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the number of transcription factors analyzed.

claim: The number of targeted eQTM methylation sites in each cell-type is 459, 3832 and 3497 in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: The number of targeted eQTM methylation sites in each cell-type is 459, 3832 and 3497 in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the number of methylation sites analyzed in TF binding site analysis.

claim: The number of TF-methylation correlation tests performed is 17,747, 209136 and 152263 in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
source_text: The number of tests performed is 17,747, 209136 and 152263 in fibroblasts, LCLs and T-cells, respectively.
